title: Policies & Disclosures

description: Privacy policy (including Google Sign-In / OAuth for Fernandes Journeys), terms of use, affiliate disclosure, comments policy, and cookies.
contentHtml:
Effective Date: September 20, 2026

This page describes how Fernandes Journeys (operated by Alex Fernandes) collects, uses, and protects information on https://www.fernandesjourneys.com. Contact: contact@fernandesjourneys.com.

  • 1. Privacy Policy
  • 1A. Google Sign-In / OAuth
  • 2. Terms of Use
  • 3. Monetization & Affiliate Disclosure

1. Privacy Policy

Who we are

Fernandes Journeys is a personal travel journal website operated by Alex Fernandes. The public site shares trip notes, destination pages, guides, and photos. It is not a travel agency and does not sell bookings as a primary product.

Controller / operator: Alex Fernandes · Email: contact@fernandesjourneys.com · Website: https://www.fernandesjourneys.com.

What the public website collects

Public visitors do not need to create an account or sign in to read stories, browse destinations, or use most of the site.

Depending on how you use the site, we may process:

  • Anonymous or aggregated analytics — visit timing, approximate location (city/region level where provided by analytics), pages viewed, and time on site, used to understand which content is useful. We do not sell individual browsing profiles.
  • Affiliate / advertising cookies — when affiliate or ad partners are active (for example Booking.com, Viator, GetYourGuide, or Google AdSense), those partners may set cookies when you click outbound links or view ads. See the Affiliate Disclosure and Cookies sections.
  • Newsletter email — if you subscribe, we collect the email address you submit (and any preference fields on the form) to send travel dispatches. You can unsubscribe via the link in each email or by contacting us.
  • Contact form messages — if you email or use a contact form, we receive the content you send so we can reply.
  • Optional Google Sign-In for readers — described in the Google Sign-In / OAuth section below (used for saving posts to your account, not required to browse).

We do not sell personal information. We do not use Google Sign-In data for advertising.

1A. Google Sign-In / OAuth (Fernandes Journeys app)

The Google Cloud OAuth application named Fernandes Journeys powers Google Sign-In on this website. Home page: https://www.fernandesjourneys.com. Privacy policy: this page (https://www.fernandesjourneys.com/policies). More about the app’s purpose: https://www.fernandesjourneys.com/app.

Purpose of Google Sign-In

Google Sign-In is used for two limited purposes on Fernandes Journeys:

  1. Optional reader accounts — any visitor may sign in with Google to save blog posts to a personal list on /account. Browsing public content does not require sign-in.
  2. Private CMS access for authorized admins only — the site owner (and any emails listed in the server allowlist) may use Google Sign-In to access the private content management system at /cms to publish and edit travel stories, pages, destinations, and media. Reader sessions alone never unlock /cms.

Fernandes Journeys is not a consumer social network or a general “login product.” Google Sign-In exists so Alex can manage the journal securely and so readers who want saved posts can do so optionally.

Data received from Google

When you sign in with Google, the site’s Auth.js / NextAuth Google provider requests the standard OpenID Connect scopes: openid, email, and profile. From Google we typically receive:

  • Email address
  • Display name
  • Profile picture URL
  • A stable Google account identifier (subject / user id) used for the session

We do not request Google Drive, Gmail, Contacts, Calendar, or other sensitive scopes.

How Google account data is used

  • Authentication and session only — to create a signed-in session cookie so the site knows who you are while you are logged in.
  • Reader saved posts — if you save posts, your Google user id is associated with those saves in our database (Firestore) so you can view and remove them later on /account.
  • CMS admin gate — for /cms, the email is checked against an allowlist of authorized admin emails (currently Alex / operators listed in server configuration). Non-admin Google accounts cannot publish content.

Google Sign-In data is not sold, not used for advertising, and not shared with unrelated third parties for marketing.

Who has access

  • Alex Fernandes (site owner) and any additional admin emails configured on the server for CMS publishing.
  • Hosting and infrastructure providers that process data as processors (see Third Parties), under their terms.

Retention and how to revoke

  • Session cookies last for the Auth.js session lifetime (or until you sign out). CMS passcode cookies (if used) are separate httpOnly cookies used only for admin unlock.
  • Saved posts remain until you remove them in Account or request deletion.
  • Revoke Google access anytime at Google Account → Security → Third-party access (or myaccount.google.com/permissions), then sign out of Fernandes Journeys.
  • To delete account-associated data we control, email contact@fernandesjourneys.com with the Google email you used.

Public visitors

You can read the entire public travel journal without Google Sign-In. Sign-in is optional for readers and required only for private CMS publishing by authorized admins.

GDPR & CCPA

If you are visiting from the European Union, UK, or California, you may have rights to access, correct, or delete personal data we hold about you. Contact contact@fernandesjourneys.com to make a request. We will respond within a reasonable time consistent with applicable law.

2. Terms of Use

By using this site, you agree to the following terms:

  • The content on this journal is for informational and entertainment purposes only. While we strive for accuracy, we cannot guarantee the completeness or timeliness of the information presented.
  • You agree to use the content for personal purposes only and not reproduce it without permission.
  • Any action you take upon the information found here is strictly at your own risk. Fernandes Journeys will not be liable for any losses or damages in connection with the use of the site.
  • Optional Google Sign-In and the private CMS are provided as-is for the purposes described in this policy. Misuse of admin tools is prohibited.

3. Monetization & Affiliate Disclosure

a. Advertising

Our site may feature ads including Google AdSense and sponsored content relevant to readers. Sponsored posts are clearly labeled and either provided by sponsors or based on personal experiences. We collaborate only with products and services that align with our values and quality standards.

b. Affiliate Marketing

This journal participates in affiliate marketing programs. When you click some links and make a purchase, we may earn a small commission at no extra cost to you. These commissions help keep the journal going.

For example, if you book a hotel through an affiliate link, the cost to you remains the same, but we may receive a commission. Affiliate partnerships do not dictate what we publish — we only recommend services we trust.

Affiliate partners may include Viator, World Nomads, GetYourGuide, Booking.com, Expedia, RentCars.com, Wise, and Babbel.

FTC Disclosure

In compliance with Federal Trade Commission guidelines, sponsored content is clearly identified. Opinions are our own, and we promote only products and services we believe in.

4. Comments Policy

  • Comments are welcome when relevant to the content.
  • A valid email address is required to comment where comments are enabled.
  • First-time comments may go through moderation; approved users’ comments may appear automatically thereafter.
  • We aim to respond to comments, especially questions, but response times vary.
  • This is not a travel agency and cannot make bookings — we can offer advice from personal experience.
  • Spam, self-promotion, defamatory, or irrelevant comments will be removed.

5. Cookies

We use cookies and similar technologies to operate the site and (where enabled) measure usage:

  • Essential / session cookies — Auth.js session cookies (authjs.session-token / __Secure-authjs.session-token) when you sign in with Google (or GitHub for CMS tooling). Optional CMS passcode cookie when an admin unlocks /cms with a passcode. Theme preference may be stored in localStorage (not a cookie).
  • Analytics — anonymous or aggregated usage statistics (visit duration, approximate location, popular content) when analytics are enabled.
  • Advertising / affiliate — partners such as Google AdSense or affiliate networks may set cookies when ads or outbound affiliate links are present.

You can disable non-essential cookies via your browser settings. Blocking essential session cookies will prevent Sign-In and CMS unlock from working.

6. Third Parties

We rely on trusted processors to run the site:

  • Vercel — hosting and edge delivery of the website.
  • Google — identity provider for Google Sign-In / OAuth (and optionally AdSense if ads are shown).
  • GitHub — source repository; CMS publishes content commits so the site can redeploy. GitHub OAuth may also be available for allowlisted CMS admins.
  • Firebase / Google Cloud Firestore — stores optional reader saved-post records keyed by authenticated user id.
  • Newsletter provider (when configured) — processes subscription emails.
  • Affiliate partners — may set cookies when you follow outbound booking or product links.

Each provider processes data under its own privacy policy. We only share what is needed to operate the features above.

7. Your Rights & Contact

To ask questions about this policy, request a copy of data we hold about you, correct it, or delete it, contact:

Alex Fernandes · Fernandes Journeys
Email: contact@fernandesjourneys.com
Web: https://www.fernandesjourneys.com

For Google Sign-In app details used in branding verification, see About this site & Google Sign-In.
